title: Carbon pathways in a terrestrial ecosystem

controls_sent.prompt:
Create an original beautiful scientific editorial ecology figure titled "Carbon pathways in a terrestrial ecosystem", landscape about 2000 × 1200, white background, muted forest green, teal, warm soil browns and soft amber. Main image is a shallow cutaway soil block with a small group of recognisable generic broadleaf plants on the LEFT, a small generic rabbit-like herbivore on the RIGHT, soil organic matter below the surface, and a magnified microbes inset at lower right. Subtle vector-friendly gradients and original detailed leaf/root/soil shapes, not a flat flowchart and not a photorealistic scene. Diagrams and labels must be scientifically clear.
At TOP, a clean rounded atmospheric reservoir labelled "Atmospheric CO₂". Exact directed CARBON fluxes: atmosphere → plants labelled "Photosynthesis"; plants → atmosphere labelled "Plant respiration"; plants → herbivore labelled "Herbivory"; herbivore → atmosphere labelled "Animal respiration"; plants → soil organic matter labelled "Litter + dead roots"; herbivore → soil organic matter labelled "Waste + remains"; soil organic matter → microbes labelled "Decomposition + uptake"; microbes → atmosphere labelled "Microbial respiration"; microbes → soil organic matter labelled "Microbial residues". Keep these nine arrows separated with short readable labels. Carbon flows, not energy: sunlight may appear as a small separate yellow downward dashed ENERGY arrow to plants only, clearly labelled "Light energy", and must not originate from the CO₂ pool. Avoid inventing transfer rates, pool sizes, emission totals, reservoirs as giant bubbles or animals breathing oxygen into CO₂ soil.
Roots stay within soil; microbes are magnified conceptual glyphs linked to the soil, not literal giant creatures. Use shapes plus labels; arrow width has no quantitative meaning. Label pools explicitly "Plant biomass", "Herbivore biomass", "Soil organic matter", "Microbial biomass". Footer "Selected terrestrial carbon pathways; not a complete budget or steady-state model. No rates, pool sizes or species-specific measurements implied." No ocean, fossil fuel infrastructure or arrows to absent reservoirs. Preserve the distinction between a stock/pool and a transfer/flux. Restrained publication aesthetic with ample whitespace; avoid crossed leaders and decorative glow.
